criteria.text: Calculates the long-stop date as 30 January 2027 (90 days after signing on 1 November 2026) and identifies that expected clearance on 16 March 2027 falls after it, recommending an extension.

Identifies that the board approval was given at a meeting with only 2 directors present when Article 11 requires a quorum of three, so the approval may be invalid, and recommends a fresh or ratifying resolution.

Identifies that the MAC carve-outs (general economic, industry-wide and pandemic changes) contain no 'disproportionate effect' exception, so the Buyer bears those risks even where the Company is disproportionately affected, and recommends adding one.
Explains how 'material adverse effect' could be read narrowly or broadly and what each reading means for the Buyer's walk-away right.
Gives the long-stop period as 90 days and as the date 30 January 2027, with days remaining from 25 November 2026 (66 days).
Includes an 'Assumptions and open questions' section listing information that is missing or should be confirmed with the client.
